The profitability of paddy cultivation and crops cultivation in dry land areas are very meager to the farming community and for which farmers prefer cash crops like Turmeric, Sugarcane, Plantation crops etc., One way of increasing the net income of the farmer is reducing the cost of cultivation. 4. The Wildlife Protection Act (1972) provides a framework for the conservation, protection and management of Wildlife. Government of Tamil Nadu has taken several initiatives in the spirit of the Wildlife Protection Act. Rescue, treatment & rehabilitation of Wild animals are critical interventions towards protection and conservation of wildlife. With increasing biotic pressure and climate change, human wildlife conflicts are bound to rise. This necessitates setting up of specialized centres with professionals to provide most appropriate rescue, treatment & rehabilitation for wildlife. Government of Tamil Nadu is committed to ensure that best possible interventions are provided for Conservation of wildlife in the State. Towards this objective, the first State-of-the-Art Rescue, Treatment & Rehabilitation Centre for wild animals shall be set up at Modur-Pethikuttai Reserve Forest in Sirumugai range in an area covering 53 hectares at a cost of Rupees 19.50 Crores (Nineteen Crores and Fifty Lakhs only).

5. It has been decided to set up the Rescue Treatment and Rehabilitation Centre at Coimbatore at Pethikuttai as it is close to areas were human wildlife conflict is reported frequently. The site is easily accessible from main road yet it provides a calm and peaceful environment for comfort and safety of wild animals. The site is well covered with green foliage to ensure adequate shade during day time. The site also has adequate water source to provide plenty of water for large animals including elephants.

3

The Rescue Treatment and Rehabilitation Centre at Coimbatore shall undertake the following activities:-

1. The Centre shall be well-equipped with trained rescue teams for conducting swift rescue operations of wild animals in distress.

2. The Centre shall provide expertise for scientific quarantine, rehabilitation & release of wild animals in identified habitats after providing necessary treatment.

3. It shall function as a leading institution for consultation & guidance to address human wildlife conflict issues.

4. The Centre shall develop and standardize protocols for rescue treatment and rehabilitation activities.

The Rescue Treatment and Rehabilitation Centre shall be divided into the following four zones:-

Human Zone:

This zone will have the administrative complex, Animal Care complex, Staff quarters, Watch tower, Store Room and Sheds etc.

Quarantine zone:

This zone will have facilities to accommodate large carnivores, birds, primates, small mammals, ungulates and reptiles. The complex can be used for quarantining a multitude of species. Since 95% of the reptiles (predominantly snakes) get released within 24 hours, all the reptilian rescue and rehabilitation activities will be confined to the quarantine zone.
